Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "could you help make this request clearer for the next cleanup-utility review. our log-file cleanup utility is used by the night operations group on the relay service, and the current run notes are hard to compare between shifts. the request is about the utility’s report and handling rules, not a change to how the relay service writes logs. we have 14 relay hosts in the group, and the same report needs to identify each host separately rather than combine all of their files under one service name. right now, a person reading the report has to open the run directory and match the host folders by hand, which is slow when a shift is checking several dates.

please ask for the report to show the host name, the log date, the file count, and the total size for each host and date. the file count should mean the number of files considered in that row, and the total size should be in megabytes, not a rounded description like “small” or “large.” the date should be the date recorded in the log name, not the time when the utility happens to run. our routine run is at 02:15, but sometimes someone starts a manual run at 11:40 in the morning, so the run time and the log date are not interchangeable. if a file name does not contain a readable date, the report should put it in a separate undated row and include the original name; it should not assign the run date as a replacement.

we also need the cleanup rule to be described in plain terms. the relay logs are kept for 45 days, counting back from the date of the run, and anything older is eligible for removal. “eligible” matters here because the utility first makes a dry-run list, and the operator checks that list before the removal step is started. we do not want the report to make it sound like files were removed just because they appear in the dry-run list. the utility currently writes that list to the run directory, but people sometimes confuse it with the record of completed removal. can the report label the two stages “planned for removal” and “removed,” and show a separate count for each stage?

one file needs to be easy to spot in that listing because the rota export is used to check who was on call during an incident. its filename is:
speaker-rota.csv
please keep the filename exactly as written, including the hyphen and the lowercase letters. when that file is older than 45 days, it should still follow the same eligibility and operator-check process as the other files; the report should not quietly make it exempt. the useful change is making the file visible by name in the report, not changing its retention rule. if it is not found in a scan, the report should not claim that it was removed or retained.

there is an archive mount used by the night group when a log needs to be retained beyond the ordinary period. the archive is not part of every run, and a missing mount should not be interpreted as an empty archive. if the archive mount is unavailable, the utility must leave the source logs in place and stop before the purge step; the report should say that the purge did not run because the archive mount was unavailable. this is important for the later check, because an operator may otherwise see an empty archive path and assume that the old files were safely copied. when the mount is available, the normal check is that the archive copy is listed before the source file is put on the removal list.

for the next review, could the request cover these specific report and run details:
1. identify the host and log date on every row, with the file count and total size in megabytes for that host-date pair;
2. put undated filenames in a separate row, retain their original names, and do not substitute the run date;
3. show the 45-day age rule as eligibility, then distinguish the dry-run plan from removal completed after operator review;
4. display speaker-rota.csv as an ordinary named file, without exempting it from the age rule or changing how a missing file is described;
5. state whether the archive mount was available, and, if it was unavailable, report that the purge did not run and that source logs remained in place.

please keep the 02:15 routine run and the 11:40 manual run as examples of why the report needs separate log-date and run-time fields, rather than turning either time into a required schedule. likewise, the 14-host figure describes the relay group we are reporting on, not a limit on how many hosts the utility can support. it would be useful if the requested wording makes those roles clear, since a reader should not mistake a sample value for a setting. the per-host rows are needed for comparing shifts, while the separate stage counts are needed for telling a planned action from a completed one.

the operators have described the current ambiguity as “the list looks like the cleanup already happened,” even on runs where the list is only a preview. please retain that concern as a reported observation, not as a claim that the utility has removed files incorrectly. another operator said, “I need to know whether the archive was checked before I look at the old logs,” which is why the mount status belongs beside the purge status in the report. these comments are from the night group’s review of the run notes; they do not establish that a particular run failed or that any data was lost.

there is also a practical issue with comparing two reports when one shift has a manual run between routine runs. the report should retain the run timestamp so people can tell which invocation they are reading, but it should group log counts by the date in each filename. if the same host has logs for several dates, those dates should remain separate instead of being rolled into one host total. a total for the whole run may be included in addition to the host-date rows, as long as it does not replace them. the request is for clearer reporting and safer interpretation of the existing steps; it is not a request to change the 45-day period, schedule an extra run, or automatically approve removals.

for the final review notes, please keep the archive condition beside the behavior it controls: when the mount is unavailable, leave source logs untouched and do not run purge; when it is available, list the archive copy before putting a source file on the removal list. the report should make those states readable without implying that availability alone confirms a successful copy. the operator’s check remains part of the process, and the distinction between a file being eligible, planned for removal, and actually removed needs to stay visible in the report. this is the detail the next shift will use when it reads the cleanup record alongside the log dates and the named files.", "output": "Could you help clarify this request for the next cleanup-utility review?
